newsitem.title: SPAIN: Banks lead Madrid stocks higher in busy trade.
newsitem.headline: Banks lead Madrid stocks higher in busy trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed sharply higher in busy trade on Wednesday, with strength in the banking sector underpinning the bourse.
Bond and currency gains also provided support as the market looked ahead to Friday's 1997 budget announcement.
The general index rose 3.26 points, 0.90 percent, to 365.04 and the Ibex-35 added 42.11 points, 1.02 percent, to 4,177.83.

Buying was concentrated in banks; BCH rose 85 pesetas to 2,825 in heavy trade, helped by forecasts of better upcoming results than in previous quarters, dealers said. Argentaria rose 120 pesetas to 5,340.
In all the outlook is optimistic short term, dealers said, with a continued run in bonds providing the focus and most expecting a cut in the Bank of Spain's key money rate next week.
"The market is firm, with more volume and possibilities of continuing the rally as long as bonds stay positive," said a dealer at Mercavalor.
Dealers said trade was led by futures, consequently boosting volume to around 43.8 billion pesetas.
